title: A short battle from my weekend Godot SRPG, with AI-assisted development
author: teamJayK
selftext:
I'm in my 50s, building Year without a Summer, a tactical RPG set in Indonesia in 1815, as a personal weekend project in Godot. This is a 13-second edit from the running demo: movement, an attack forecast, an attack, and a counterattack. The current UI is in Korean.



I use Codex and Claude for coding, and AI tools for parts of the art and animation workflow. I started the project with my own character sketches and storyboards on a Galaxy S23 Ultra, using Sketchbook and FlipaClip. Art, animation, and integrating everything into the game have taken more work than I first expected.



For this recording, Codex used the game's existing automation hooks to move a unit and resolve a normal attack and counterattack, while Godot's MovieMaker recorded the running game. The first capture stalled on battle dialogue; advancing it through the normal game flow fixed the recording. The clip is trimmed at normal speed, downscaled, and watermarked. It uses the normal combat logic and unchanged battle stats.



I'm still tuning balance and readability. Does the move-to-forecast-to-attack/counter sequence read clearly at this pace? I used AI assistance to draft and translate this post.
